overclaims: The company announcement supplies run-rate context, while articles repeating the exact comparison trace back to Zitron.
checks.note: The rationale says 'articles' (plural) repeat the comparison and trace back to Zitron. Only one article (OSNews) was read, it was marked unused, and it is not an evidence item, so the evidence items don't support this sentence. The proposition ends with 'more than 100% of its revenue', but the speaker said 'estimated revenue'. The estimate qualifier does appear in the conditions. e1's excerpt, dates and relation are correct. The outcome (unresolved, horizon not applicable) matches the agreed assessment.

GPT-5.2 (2025-12-11) and GPT-5.4 (2026-03-05) are each priced above their predecessors, both within six months of publication. Sonnet 4.6 kept its price. The criteria show the interpretation of 'next few months' (three-month and six-month readings) and the imposed-versus-optional distinction. The cloning remark in the excerpt is explicitly excluded from assessment. The horizon has elapsed by 2026-10-28, so the stated outcome (elapsed, unresolved) matches the agreed assessment. The citation excerpts are exact substrings of the sources.

The proposition keeps both the scope ('the data seen' for Anthropic and Cursor) and the qualifier 'overall direction'. The rationale correctly says the filing covers a different measure (expenses across all providers) and period (full-year 2025). Each company's reporting window is shown. e4's excerpt, publisher and dates (available 2026-10-26) are correct. The outcome (unresolved) matches the agreed assessment.
